topics.title: Mijbil and the author's care for him

concepts.learning_objective: Recall where otters like Mijbil come from and the setting of the author's home.
Identify the arrangements and care the author provided for his pet otter.
Link Mijbil's actions to the emotions they show.

topics.title: Reading Text I: Baby Bhakat, the civet cat

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the features and habits of the civet cat described in the passage.
Recall details of Bhakat's rescue, home and human family.
Infer how a wild animal helps maintain the balance of life in nature.
State why humans and wildlife increasingly come into conflict.
Describe the impact of the conflict on people and animals.
Evaluate simple solutions that lead to mutually beneficial coexistence.
Explain what it means that animals have an inherent worth and can feel.
Distinguish equal consideration from equal treatment of animals.
Interpret how everyday choices can work as non-violent protest.

topics.title: Vocabulary: synonyms and words used as nouns and verbs

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the word that is not a synonym in a group of words.
Distinguish the use of the same word as a noun and as a verb.

topics.title: Grammar: noun modifiers, -ed/-ing adjectives, would and used to

concepts.learning_objective: Combine sentences using adjectives and adjective phrases as noun modifiers.
Choose correctly between -ed and -ing forms of adjectives.
Use 'would' and 'used to' correctly for repeated past actions and past states.
Apply capital letters, commas, full stops and inverted commas correctly.
Rearrange jumbled parts into a meaningful, punctuated sentence.
Recall factual details from the listening text about Gangaram.
Interpret the story as an example of humans and animals living together.
